vopros: Should I pay for a tool that tracks whether ChatGPT and other AI assistants mention my business, or hire someone to get my business recommended by AI?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Short answer: **these are two different jobs, and most businesses eventually need a bit of both — but you should think about them separately rather than assuming you need to pay for either right away.**

Here's the breakdown:

## Tracking tools (monitoring) vs. GEO services (action)

**Tracking tools** just tell you what's happening — whether ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini mention you, how often, in what context, and how you compare to competitors. Tools like Otterly, Profound, Peec AI, Siftly, SE Ranking, and Semrush's checker run your buyers' prompts through ChatGPT on a schedule and record every time your brand is named, beating manual checking because ChatGPT's answers vary run to run. That last point matters: ChatGPT's answers are non-deterministic — they vary by phrasing, context, and model updates, which is why reliable tracking requires repeated sampling, not one check.

**"GEO" (Generative Engine Optimization) services** are the doing side — the practice of optimizing your business's web presence so AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews mention and recommend it in their answers. Agencies and consultants in this space focus on things like getting your business mentioned in third-party comparison articles and listicles, keeping your name, description, and services identical everywhere online, maintaining active review profiles, and publishing statistics-dense, quotable content.

## Practical guidance for deciding

**Start with free/cheap tracking, not a paid tool or a hire.** Before spending anything, you can literally ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc. "best [your industry] in [your city]" a bunch of times yourself and see what comes up — you can ask ChatGPT directly and see if you appear, but you'd need to repeat it many times, across many phrasings, to get a reliable read. Several tools also offer free tiers to baseline your ChatGPT visibility before you pay for anything.

**Only pay for a tracking tool if:**
- You've done the manual check and found it genuinely time-consuming to repeat regularly
- You have competitors and want ongoing comparison data, not a one-time snapshot
- You need sentiment/citation-source data to actually diagnose *why* you're missing (many tools bundle this — the basics should include mentions, position, citations, and sentiment so you understand what ChatGPT says, how visible you are, and what sources influence the answer)

**Only hire someone for GEO if:**
- Tracking has already shown you a real problem (you're absent or mischaracterized on prompts that matter to your revenue)
- You don't have the in-house time/skill to fix the underlying issues yourself — which, notably, overlap heavily with things you may already control cheaply: reviews, consistent business info (NAP), getting listed in relevant comparison/listicle content, and clear, factual on-site content
- You're a larger business where a few percentage points of AI-driven visibility translate into meaningful revenue (the case is much weaker for a small, local, low-ticket business)

**A caution:** GEO is a very new, unproven field — it has not been the subject of enough research to develop a shared understanding of its best practices among marketing professionals, though the literature is expected to grow the way SEO's did. That means many "GEO agencies" are selling confidence, not certainty. Be skeptical of anyone promising guaranteed mentions or fast rankings-style ROI — the mechanics (and how much they matter to your specific business) are still being figured out in real time.

## Bottom line
Don't pay for a monitoring tool as a first move just to "see" a problem you could check manually in an afternoon. And don't hire a GEO consultant before you have data showing you actually have a visibility problem worth fixing. The sane order is: **manually spot-check → if it looks like an ongoing issue worth watching, get a low-cost tracking tool (or free tier) → if data shows a real, revenue-relevant gap, then consider paying someone (or DIY-ing) the fixes**, many of which are basic reputation/content hygiene you may not need an outside "AI expert" for at all.
